author: The Comfort Kitchen
title: Southern Fried Pork Chops and Gravy Taste Like Sunday Supper
text:
1 days ago Southern Fried Pork Chops deliver a crunchy seasoned crust, juicy meat, and homemade gravy in every forkful. Bone-in chops are dipped in buttermilk and coated with flour flavored with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt, and pepper. Pan-frying creates crisp golden edges while preserving the moisture inside. Once the chops are finished, butter, flour, chicken broth, and milk or cream turn the skillet drippings into a velvety gravy. Spooned across the top, it settles into the breading without completely hiding the satisfying crunch beneath it.
Photo by Letisha Uber Serve the chops with mashed potatoes, biscuits, green beans, collard greens, corn, or macaroni and cheese for a full Southern-style dinner. Let excess buttermilk drip away before breading, press the flour firmly onto the meat, and avoid crowding the skillet so the oil temperature remains steady. A cast-iron pan is especially good at maintaining heat and developing an even crust. The gravy can be seasoned with extra pepper, herbs, or a pinch of cayenne depending on the table. This recipe belongs at family dinners, Sunday suppers, and cold evenings when something hearty is required. Leftovers reheat well, but that combination of crispy pork and hot skillet gravy rarely leaves much behind.
